previous_digest_file: 2026-08-29 - Weekly Portable Audio DSP GitHub Digest.md

top_repos.portability_reason: The reusable q_lib headers are separable from q_io audio-device, stream, and file code, but templates and memory behavior still need Cortex-M7 profiling.
top_repos.value_reason: Q's q_lib contributes reusable biquads, delay lines, envelopes, oscillators, and pitch utilities without requiring its q_io device layer.
top_repos.port_idea: Start with q_lib biquad, delay, envelope, and oscillator headers; replace q_io with fixed board callbacks and benchmark template size plus denormal behavior.
top_repos.note: Re-entry: updated - Q's q_lib contributes reusable biquads, delay lines, envelopes, oscillators, and pitch utilities without requiring its q_io device layer.
top_repos.summary: C++ Library for Audio Digital Signal Processing

top_repos.portability_reason: Instrument tick functions are platform-independent C++, but many delay classes allocate during construction and STK's file, socket, mutex, RtAudio, and RtMidi layers must be left out.
top_repos.value_reason: STK's MIT C++ classes cover mature digital-waveguide and modal instruments including clarinet tone-hole/vent geometry, plucked strings, modal bars, and a two-dimensional waveguide mesh.
top_repos.port_idea: Extract one instrument such as BlowHole or ModalBar, replace StkError/file and RtAudio hooks, pre-size every delay at setup, and run the single-sample tick path in the board callback.
top_repos.note: Returning - STK's MIT C++ classes cover mature digital-waveguide and modal instruments including clarinet tone-hole/vent geometry, plucked strings, modal bars, and a two-dimensional waveguide mesh.
top_repos.summary: The Synthesis ToolKit in C++: portable audio processing and algorithmic synthesis classes.

top_repos.portability_reason: The crate explicitly supports no_std and stack AudioNode graphs, but some nodes require alloc and its 64-sample block path assumes wide SIMD that is not a Cortex-M7 drop-in.
top_repos.value_reason: FunDSP provides Apache-licensed no_std Rust AudioNode graphs, stack-backed fixed-arity processing, analytic linear-network responses, and a broad oscillator/filter/envelope toolkit.
top_repos.port_idea: Build a no_std static AudioNode graph with default features disabled, keep 32-bit scalar tick processing first, and exclude AudioUnit, files, FFT convolution, heap-backed buffers, and explicit wide SIMD.
top_repos.note: Returning - FunDSP provides Apache-licensed no_std Rust AudioNode graphs, stack-backed fixed-arity processing, analytic linear-network responses, and a broad oscillator/filter/envelope toolkit.
top_repos.summary: Rust library for audio processing and synthesis with static and dynamic graph systems.

top_repos.portability_reason: Individual delay, diffusion, feedback, and distortion processors are separable, while the growable recursive node graph and multi-mode delay store are unsuitable for a fixed MCU build.
top_repos.value_reason: The BSD delay core combines modulated variable interpolation, diffusion, pitch/reverse modes, feedback filtering, and nonlinear processing as independently visible DSP blocks.
top_repos.port_idea: Freeze one or two DelayProc nodes into a fixed topology, keep one interpolation mode, allocate each delay from a measured static arena, and omit the recursive editor-controlled node tree.
top_repos.note: Returning - The BSD delay core combines modulated variable interpolation, diffusion, pitch/reverse modes, feedback filtering, and nonlinear processing as independently visible DSP blocks.
top_repos.summary: Matrix delay effect built from a growable tree of independently controlled delay lines.

top_repos.portability_reason: The algorithms are readable and modest, but most DSP state and rendering lives inside JUCE AudioProcessor implementations and the legacy code lacks parameter dezippering.
top_repos.value_reason: The MIT collection exposes heavily commented classic MDA algorithms, including JX10 and DX10 synth voices, EPiano, RezFilter, SubSynth, dynamics, delay, and spectral-free effects.
top_repos.port_idea: Start with the JX10 voice or RezFilter loop, move DSP state out of AudioProcessor, replace JUCE MIDI/buffers with fixed callbacks, and add parameter dezippering omitted by the legacy code.
top_repos.note: Returning - The MIT collection exposes heavily commented classic MDA algorithms, including JX10 and DX10 synth voices, EPiano, RezFilter, SubSynth, dynamics, delay, and spectral-free effects.
top_repos.summary: Commented JUCE implementations of the classic MDA synth and effect algorithms.

top_repos.portability_reason: The kick stages are clean DSP classes, but they currently depend on JUCE/chowdsp buffers, smoothed parameters, and XSIMD nonlinear vector math.
top_repos.value_reason: The BSD source separates a pulse shaper, trigger, output filter, and resonant kick circuit with selectable nonlinear tanh feedback corrections derived from old drum-machine models.
top_repos.port_idea: Extract the scalar pulse-plus-resonant-filter chain, replace JUCE/chowdsp parameter blocks and XSIMD vectors, and update pitch, tightness, and bounce only at control rate.
top_repos.note: Returning - The BSD source separates a pulse shaper, trigger, output filter, and resonant kick circuit with selectable nonlinear tanh feedback corrections derived from old drum-machine models.
top_repos.summary: Kick synthesizer based on creative modelling of old-school drum machine circuits.

top_repos.portability_reason: Effects are exposed as reusable C++ headers, but delay-backed modules allocate at configure time and frequency shifting/reverb pull in separate Hilbert or DSP submodules.
top_repos.value_reason: The MIT reusable headers supply a Hilbert/Bode frequency shifter, Householder FDN reverb, chorus, limiter, analyser, and crunch effect behind configure/process/reset interfaces.
top_repos.port_idea: Port chorus or limiter first, replace configure-time dynamic storage with bounded arrays, then budget the eight-line FDN and leave analyser/STFT modules out of the first firmware build.
top_repos.note: Returning - The MIT reusable headers supply a Hilbert/Bode frequency shifter, Householder FDN reverb, chorus, limiter, analyser, and crunch effect behind configure/process/reset interfaces.
top_repos.summary: Reusable MIT C++ chorus, crunch, frequency shifter, limiter, analyser, and reverb classes.

top_repos.portability_reason: Module compute functions are compact scalar C, but the create/init lifecycle uses heap allocation and the full library includes file, FFT, convolution, and desktop audio dependencies.
top_repos.value_reason: Soundpipe's MIT C modules offer single-sample callbacks for physical-model percussion, Moog ladder, pluck, variable delay, granular and Csound/Faust-derived effects with independent create/init/compute lifecycles.
top_repos.port_idea: Select one module such as drip or moogladder, replace create/init malloc with caller-owned structs and buffers, and omit file, FFT, Paulstretch, convolution, and JACK modules.
top_repos.note: Returning - Soundpipe's MIT C modules offer single-sample callbacks for physical-model percussion, Moog ladder, pluck, variable delay, granular and Csound/Faust-derived effects with independent create/init/compute lifecycles.
top_repos.summary: A lightweight C music DSP library with independent single-sample processing modules.

top_repos.portability_reason: DSP evidence is already visible in portable source paths with little host/UI coupling.
top_repos.value_reason: The Faust core models a Small-Stone-style four-all-pass phaser with color-dependent sweep ranges, feedback bass cut, and a stereo LFO phase offset.
top_repos.port_idea: Generate the mono Faust kernel first, keep the four all-pass stages and feedback HPF, then add the stereo phase-offset path only after profiling.
top_repos.note: Returning - The Faust core models a Small-Stone-style four-all-pass phaser with color-dependent sweep ranges, feedback bass cut, and a stereo LFO phase offset.
top_repos.summary: A classic analog phaser effect, made with DPF and Faust

top_repos.portability_reason: Its per-sample DSP is bounded and separated from JUCE, but the full 8-16 voice, dual-exciter, three-resonator, effects and 2x/4x configuration is too large; a reduced mono voice is the realistic target.
top_repos.value_reason: AERIFORM's MIT DSP layer combines dual exciters, PolyBLEP/chaotic/noise and physical sources with three cross-fed resonators, bounded feedback, fixed 12-mode banks, and allocation-free 2x/4x IIR oversampling.
top_repos.port_idea: Port one exciter into one 5-12 mode resonator at 1x, retain the finite/energy governor, and add a second resonator or oversampling only after SRAM and cycle measurements.
top_repos.note: New - AERIFORM's MIT DSP layer combines dual exciters, PolyBLEP/chaotic/noise and physical sources with three cross-fed resonators, bounded feedback, fixed 12-mode banks, and allocation-free 2x/4x IIR oversampling.
top_repos.summary: Oscillator-free physical-modelling synth with dual exciters and a three-resonator feedback network.
